//: Per section 8. Components are released TOGETHER on one shared release branch, but keep
INDEPENDENT versions -- a release event bumps several components at once, it does not give
them one shared number. That is projectsRelationship: independent, not fixed.
currentVersionResolver: git-tag, with disk as the fallback. The current version of a
component is what was last RELEASED, which is exactly what its component/version tag
records, and it is also what section 8's changed-set rule is phrased against: changed since
its own last component/version tag. The registry -- Nx's npm default -- is the wrong source
here, because section 6 targets rung 1 and nothing publishes from a dev branch, so the
registry has nothing to say. disk covers the first release, before any tag exists.
specifierSource and currentVersionResolver are spelled out rather than using the
version.conventionalCommits shorthand: that shorthand also pins currentVersionResolver, and
setting both is a hard error -- Nx refuses with 'you have configured both the shorthand and
one or more of the related configuration options'.
preserveLocalDependencyProtocols keeps `workspace:^` in the tree. This is load-bearing and
not cosmetic: the whole ordering argument in section 8 rests on pnpm rewriting that range at
PUBLISH time from the version already sitting in the dependency's package.json. If Nx
rewrote it to a fixed version at version time, release-finish would go back to being
order-sensitive and every version bump would churn 100 dependency ranges.
updateDependents: auto is the step that used to be done by hand, base components first.

//preVersionCommand: Refuses a real release from any branch but `main`. Nx runs this FIRST -- before versioning,
the commit, the tag and the push -- and a non-zero exit aborts the whole command with nothing
done. Compare the missing-token failure, which lands AFTER the push and cannot be retried
because the tag is already consumed.
A pre-push git hook was the obvious alternative and does not work: nx pushes with
--no-verify, so pre-push never fires. It would have been a safeguard that silently does
Dry runs are allowed -- nx sets NX_DRY_RUN=true here and the guard honours it. Reading the
plan from `release` before promoting writes nothing and gives the same answer.

//: The release notes live as GitHub Releases, one per component, not as CHANGELOG.md files
in the tree. `file: false` stops the file being written; `createRelease: github` publishes
the same generated notes against the component/version tag.
Nothing is lost at the consumer end: no package listed CHANGELOG.md in its `files`, so it
was never in a published tarball. The 11 files nx had generated were deleted with this
change. The three components that carried an UPSTREAM changelog from their own repository
-- class-view, graphapi, jest-chrome-in-docker-environment -- keep it, restored to its
pre-release content: nx had prepended a generated section to a file it did not author, and
that history belongs to the component, not to this workspace. vscode's is untouched; it is
not in the release set at all.
workspaceChangelog stays false, and now it MUST: nx cannot create GitHub Releases for both
project changelogs and the workspace changelog, and this workspace releases per component.
AUTH: export GH_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)" before releasing. An earlier version of this comment
said no setup was needed because nx falls back to the gh CLI. Measured on 2026-09-10 and that
is false on Windows: nx looks for ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, while gh keeps it in the Roaming
AppData "GitHub CLI" folder. Nx never finds it, never runs `gh auth token`, calls the API
unauthenticated and gets a 401 -- AFTER the commit, tag and push have already succeeded -- then
opens an interactive browser prompt. Re-running does not repair it: the tag is consumed, so the
next run sees no new conventional commits.
PUSH: nx pushes the current branch BEFORE creating the releases, and that order is required
rather than incidental -- it sends GitHub a tag name plus a target commit, so the commit must
already be on the remote. It is NOT requested by --git-push: the combined `nx release` command
ignores that flag and pushes if and only if a release group is configured to create a remote
release, which createRelease above makes true. Only the `version` and `changelog` subcommands
read the flag. Stand on `main` when you run it.
